:::{#def-poisson-regression}
#### Poisson regression model

Let $Y$ be a count outcome,
$\vX$ a [covariate vector](correlation-regression.qmd#def-slr-covariate-vector),
and $T$ the [exposure magnitude](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-exposure)
over which the [events](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-event) in $Y$ are counted.
A **Poisson regression model** assumes that,
given $\vX = \vx$ and $T = t$,
$Y$ has a [Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson)

$$Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t \sim \Pois(\mu(\vx, t))$$

whose mean is the [event](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-event) rate $\lambda(\vx)$ multiplied by the exposure,
with the [log](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-natural-log) of the event rate equal to a linear [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-function) of the [covariates](model-validation.qmd#def-covariate):

$$
\ba
\E{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t} &= \mu(\vx,t) \\
\mu(\vx,t) &\eqdef \lambda(\vx)\cdot t \\
\lambda(\vx) &\eqdef \exp{\eta(\vx)} \\
\eta(\vx) &\eqdef \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \dots + \beta_p x_p
\ea
$${#eq-mean-poisson}

:::
